claim.statement: Current AWS security documentation says Kiro can read, create, modify, search and delete files and run filesystem-impacting commands in both Autopilot and Supervised modes, while protected paths require explicit approval.

source.title: Kiro privacy and security
source.locator: Autopilot versus supervised mode and Protected paths

limitations: This is a publisher description, not an observed permission-enforcement receipt for 1.0.242.
unknowns: Workspace, target paths, operation mode, command policy and approval results are unknown.

claim.statement: Current AWS documentation distinguishes Autopilot, where changes can be applied without per-step approval, from Supervised, where Kiro yields after a turn containing file edits for hunk or file review; both retain interrupt and revert paths.

source.title: Kiro Autopilot
source.locator: How it works and change management features

limitations: Supervised review follows tool writes to disk and is not evidence that no pre-review filesystem mutation occurs.
unknowns: The effective mode, pending changes, checkpoints and review decisions are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro terminal documentation says commands require approval by default, can be run once or added to a prefix-based trusted list, and can be forced back to manual review by a substring-based command denylist.

limitations: Prefix trust applies to an entire command string and does not establish semantic analysis of chains, pipes or redirects.
unknowns: Trusted and denied patterns, proposed commands, modifications, approvals and outputs are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro MCP documentation says configured servers can expose tools, Kiro can select them, tools request approval by default, named tools may be auto-approved, and servers or individual tools may be disabled.

limitations: MCP servers are external components with their own authority and are not identified by the Kiro client version.
unknowns: Servers, transport, tools, schemas, parameters, credentials, disabled lists and approvals are unknown.

releaseContext.statement: AWS published Kiro IDE 1.0.242 on 2026-07-28 and identified Code OSS 1.108.2 as its editor base. Platform installer digests and rolling service revisions remain unresolved.

propositions.question: Which Kiro IDE release is pinned?
propositions.answer: The publisher identifies 1.0.242 and Code OSS 1.108.2; no platform digest is known.
propositions.whyItMatters: A desktop version does not identify a particular installer or service backend.

propositions.question: Which platform and model service applied?
propositions.answer: Platform installer, model selection, provider region and service revision remain unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: Desktop and hosted identities are independent applicability boundaries.

propositions.question: When are file changes reviewed?
propositions.answer: Current docs distinguish immediate application from turn-level hunk review, while protected paths retain an explicit prompt.
propositions.whyItMatters: The same tool capabilities have different review workflows.

propositions.question: Which actions can run automatically?
propositions.answer: Commands and MCP tools have separate manual, trusted, denied, disabled and auto-approved paths.
propositions.whyItMatters: Tool authority cannot be inferred from operation mode alone.

propositions.question: Which spec approval chain applies?
propositions.answer: Quick Spec removes inter-phase approval gates; standard workflows retain review stages.
propositions.whyItMatters: A named planning surface does not imply one approval sequence.

propositions.question: Can events invoke actions?
propositions.answer: Current docs describe event-triggered agent prompts and local shell commands.
propositions.whyItMatters: Event-driven authority depends on trigger and action configuration.

propositions.question: Was Kiro IDE 1.0.242 independently evaluated here?
propositions.answer: No exact-build evaluation passed into this dossier.
propositions.whyItMatters: Publisher documentation is attribution, not observed behavior.

boundaries.note: Unpublished public-source attribution only; exact desktop identity remains separate from rolling service and effective authority configuration.
